title: Routing resolver rewrite: unified selector for region/tier and graceful fallback variants
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Current routing rules are fragmented across multiple interpreters (region selector, tier allocator, fallback mapper). This causes correctness gaps: inconsistent fallbacks across regions, inability to express cost/latency weightings, and brittle upgrades when we introduce new model variants or quantized backends.

Goal: Implement a single, well-documented routing resolver that validates a compact DSL schema, resolves an ordered decision graph for region + tier selection, and emits deterministic fallback model variants. The resolver must be incrementally deployable (compatibility shim + feature flag), observable, and fast (p95 resolution < 3ms for cached policies).
acceptance_criteria: A unified routing resolver binary is added to routing-engine service and passes CI integration tests
New DSL schema defined in schema/v2/routing-policy.schema.yaml with compatibility rules and published docs
Staged migration tool that translates legacy policy JSON -> new DSL is available and validated against 5 representative customer policies
Metrics emitted: routing_resolution_ms, routing_fallback_invocations, routing_miss_rate, resolver_eval_count
Canary rollout option implemented to enable resolver per-team (console flag + API header)
No user-visible change in behavior for existing policies when compatibility shim is enabled
technical_notes: Design summary: 1) Parse policy DSL into a typed intermediate representation (IR) that separates selection predicates (region, latency, cost, data residency) from route actions (model variant, tier, affinity). 2) Implement deterministic resolver that evaluates predicates in a prioritized sequence and produces a ranked candidate list with explicit fallback links. 3) Provide a validation pass that enforces invariants (e.g. every tier route must have at least one compatible model variant, region outputs must have an explicit fallback). 4) Performance: use memoized predicate evaluation and compact IR to allow hot-path evaluation under 100ns per predicate for cached inputs. 5) Backcompat: build a transpiler from legacy policy keys to the new DSL with non-destructive roundtrip tests.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Add resolver behind feature flag; routing-engine exposes new /resolve_v2 endpoint. Keep /resolve_v1 active.
Phase 2: Run migration tool on a copy of customer policies; run canonicalizer and linter producing a report of issues per policy.
Phase 3: Canary 5% of internal traffic through /resolve_v2 for non-critical customers; compare outputs vs v1 and record diffs.
Phase 4: Address diffs and add compatibility shims; expand canary to 25% then 100% for selected tenants.
Phase 5: Deprecate v1 after 8 weeks of zero-severity diffs and sign-off from PG and infra teams.
rollout_steps: Create feature flag in console: resolver_v2_enable
Deploy routing-engine with resolver_v2 behind flag to staging
Run automated policy corpus smoke tests and property-based tests in staging
Enable flag for internal tenants and monitor metrics for 72h
Open limited external canary and collect customer feedback
Progressively enable for all tenants and mark v1 deprecated
Ship migration docs and CLI helper to customers
test_plan: Unit: grammar->AST->IR roundtrip for 1000 randomized DSL samples
Integration: end-to-end routing resolution against sample traffic replay (latency and correctness)
Property tests: invariants for fallback reachability and termination
Benchmark: p50/p95/p99 resolution time with 10k concurrent evaluations
Regression: compare outputs of resolve_v2 vs resolve_v1 for the customer policy corpus and flag diffs > 0.1%
notes: Follow-up tasks: add interactive console view for resolved candidate trees; pair with Perf infra on kernel selection signals if resolver starts influencing hardware choices. Reach out to Solutions Eng before broad rollout for customers with strict residency constraints.
